reading.passageText: A city health department launched a pilot scheme that marked short walking routes between transport hubs, clinics and shopping streets. The project was not designed simply as a tourism feature. Instead, planners wanted to encourage small amounts of daily movement among residents who said they had no time for formal exercise. Local clinics supported the scheme because many patients with early signs of lifestyle-related illness felt intimidated by gyms or could not commit to structured fitness programmes. Doctors argued that short, repeated walks integrated into normal routines were more realistic for these patients than ambitious exercise plans that were quickly abandoned.
